Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on the oceans. Because the Earth rotates, most coastlines see two high tides and two low tides roughly every 24 hours and 50 minutes. The Sun pulls on the oceans too, though less strongly than the Moon. Can you summarise this paragraph for me?

Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on the oceans. Because the Earth rotates, most coastlines see two high tides and two low tides roughly every 24 hours and 50 minutes. The Sun pulls on the oceans too, though less strongly than the Moon. When the Sun and Moon line up, at new and full moon, their effects add together and produce larger 'spring' tides. When they sit at right angles, the effects partly cancel, giving smaller 'neap' tides. The shape of a coastline can make the range much bigger or smaller.
turns.reply: Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused primarily by the Moon's gravity and secondarily by the Sun. Depending on the alignment of these celestial bodies and the shape of the coastline, this results in varying high and low tides, known as spring and neap tides.
